name: Seated Soleus Raise with Pause
description: A seated calf raise performed with a deliberate pause at the top of the movement (maximum plantarflexion), increasing time-under-tension for the soleus muscle. Because the seated position with bent knees isolates the soleus from the gastrocnemius, this exercise is particularly effective for Achilles tendinopathy rehabilitation at the soleus-tendon junction, distal Achilles insertional issues, and plantar fasciitis programs. The pause amplifies the therapeutic loading stimulus at the top.

execution.starting_position: Sit on a bench or chair with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees. Place a dumbbell or weight plate on the thighs just above the knees. Position the balls of the feet on the edge of a small block or plate for full range.
execution.setup_instructions: The key setup requirement is a 90-degree (or greater) knee angle, which disables the gastrocnemius and isolates the soleus. Use a step or block under the forefeet for maximum range.
steps: Step 1: Begin with heels lowered below the forefeet for the full stretch position.
Step 2: Press through the balls of the feet to rise to the full plantarflexed (tiptoe) position.
Step 3: PAUSE at the top for 2-3 seconds, maintaining maximum plantarflexion and squeezing the soleus.
Step 4: Lower slowly (3-4 seconds) back to the full stretch. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you rise. Breathe during the top pause. Inhale slowly as you lower.
common_mistakes: Skipping the pause — the pause is what differentiates this from a standard seated calf raise
Partial range at the top — rise to true maximum plantarflexion
Rushing the eccentric — 3-4 second lowering is prescribed
safety_considerations: For insertional Achilles tendinopathy, do not let the heel drop below the level of the forefoot — this can aggravate the insertion
For mid-portion tendinopathy, full range is typically better tolerated and therapeutically indicated
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full dorsiflexion to full plantarflexion. The pause occurs at maximum plantarflexion.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2s raise, 3s pause at top, 3s slow eccentric lower
coaching_cues: Feel the deep calf (soleus) hold the pause at the top — not the gastrocnemius (which is inactive at 90-degree knee angle)
Squeeze the calf hard during the pause
Let the heel drop for the full stretch — feel the tension through the lower calf and Achilles
